sources.cite: Kyle Bradbury and Nick Eubank, Practical Data Science with Python, 'Validating a merge'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: validate 'will accept "1:1", "1:m", "m:1", and "m:m"' and 'will then check to make sure your merge matches the type of merge you think it is'; with indicator=True pandas adds a _merge column marking each row as from both, left only or right only; if a key you assumed unique appears twice, 'you'll end up with two observations for each value after the merge'. The page did not name the exception; pandas raises MergeError (to verify against the pandas reference, not opened for this round).
Corner Market Co-op, its stores, orders, totals and deadline are invented teaching values; notebook output is an authored rendering. 1,512 orders of store 14 counted twice add 90,350 to 2,914,600.

brief.situation: You run the monthly revenue notebook at Corner Market Co-op (fictional). October's regional revenue totals 3,004,950, while the till system says 2,914,600. Store 14 moved from the North region to Harbor in September. The board pack locks at 11:00. It is 10:10.
handover: orders.parquet has one row per order (48,210 in October).
region_lookup.csv maps each store_id to its region; whoever updated it for store 14 added a row.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: inspect the data, change the merge, run the checks, or send the figures. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Sending is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

scoring.modelReasoning: A left merge onto a lookup should keep one row per order; 49,722 rows from 48,210 orders says some key matched twice. Store 14 has two lookup rows after its move, so its 1,512 orders were counted in both regions (90,350 extra). Keep each store's latest row and merge with validate="m:1" and indicator=True, so a duplicate raises MergeError instead of inflating figures. drop_duplicates on the result removes nothing because the copies differ in region, and deleting the store's orders destroys real data. Reconcile rows and revenue with the tills before sending.
